title: Gemini CLI shell expansion can bypass read-only command approval checks
summary: Gemini CLI can upgrade a shell command from ASK_USER to ALLOW using its unexpanded text. Bash can then expand arguments into destructive or execution-capable find flags that the classifier did not inspect. Version 0.70.0 includes the merged fix that preserves confirmation for unresolved expansions.

severity.rationale: An agent processing untrusted project content can be induced to request commands that cross the shell approval boundary. Code execution still requires the agent to emit such a command, a common precondition in coding-agent workflows.

affected.note: Tagged 0.69.0 source contains the vulnerable classification path. The earliest affected release is not established by the inspected sources.

exposure: Applies to Bash shell-command classification when default confirmation would be upgraded because the command appears read-only. The fix does not revoke explicit ALLOW rules or deliberately bypassed approval modes. PowerShell behavior is outside this record.

params.instructions: Check the installed @google/gemini-cli version and shell policy. Version 0.69.0 is confirmed affected; upgrade to 0.70.0 or a later release containing the unresolved-expansion guard. Earlier versions need source inspection.

remediation.details: Install 0.70.0 or a later release containing the fix for unresolved shell expansion. Review explicit shell ALLOW rules separately, since the fix intentionally preserves them.
remediation.risk: Medium. Additional confirmation prompts can interrupt unattended workflows.

verification: Confirm the installed version and that the policy engine retains ASK_USER when a nominally read-only command contains unresolved Bash expansion.
Test policy decisions with harmless expansion examples in an isolated workspace; do not use destructive commands as a recovery check.

review.notes: Independent reviewer re-read every tier 1 source and checked every field. No open findings.

history.change: Initial record from the merged vendor fix, release notes and directly inspected vulnerable and patched tagged source. No CVE, vendor severity or exploitation status asserted.
